title: Senior Financial Analyst, FP&A
description:
About the Company



Spectrum Building Services of America is a growing commercial facilities services company serving major national and regional customers across multiple U.S. markets.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Financial Analyst, FP&A to join our finance team. This is not a bookkeeping or data-entry position. We are looking for someone who enjoys understanding the story behind the numbers, investigating why financial results changed, building financial models, and turning financial and operational data into useful information for management.

The successful candidate will work closely with the CEO, accounting team, and operational leadership to provide accurate, timely, and insightful financial analysis.



Position Summary

The Senior Financial Analyst will be responsible for financial planning and analysis, management reporting, budgeting, forecasting, financial statement analysis, profitability analysis, cash-flow forecasting, and financial modeling.

A major responsibility of this position is cause-of-change and root-cause analysis.

We do not simply want reports showing that an expense increased or profitability declined. We expect the analyst to investigate the underlying data, determine what caused the change, quantify the major drivers, identify items requiring further investigation, and clearly communicate the findings.



You should be comfortable receiving financial information and independently asking:

• What changed?

• Why did it change?

• Does the result make sense?

• Is this an accounting issue or an actual business result?

• What are the major drivers?

• What should management pay attention to?



Key Responsibilities

Financial Statement Analysis

• Perform monthly P&L analysis comparing actual results to budget, forecast, prior month, and prior year.

• Perform balance-sheet analysis and identify unusual or unexplained changes.

• Prepare monthly cause-of-change and variance analyses.

• Investigate significant financial variances to determine underlying drivers.

• Identify potential accounting errors or inconsistencies and work with the accounting team to investigate and resolve them.

• Prepare concise management explanations of financial performance.



Budgeting & Forecasting

• Support preparation of the annual company budget.

• Maintain rolling financial forecasts.

• Update forecasts based on actual results and changing business assumptions.

• Build revenue, labor, supply, overhead, EBITDA, and cash-flow forecasts.

• Maintain forecast models and supporting schedules.

• Compare actual results against forecasts and explain significant differences.



Cash-Flow Forecasting

• Prepare and maintain short- and medium-term cash-flow forecasts.

• Analyze expected customer receipts, payroll, vendor payments, taxes, capital expenditures, and other cash requirements.

• Identify potential cash-flow risks and significant changes in expected cash position.



Profitability Analysis

Analyze profitability by:

• Customer

• Contract

• Market/geography

• Business unit

• Other relevant operating segments



Identify the primary drivers of profitability changes, including:

• Labor hours

• Wage rates

• Overtime

• Supplies

• Pricing

• Revenue changes

• Operating expenses

• Productivity



Month-End Close & Management Reporting

Work with the accounting team during month-end close to:

• Review preliminary financial results.

• Perform analytical review of the P&L and balance sheet.

• Identify unusual balances or transactions.

• Prepare supporting financial schedules.

• Track questions and exceptions requiring accounting investigation.

• Confirm that identified issues have been addressed before management reporting is finalized.

• Prepare the monthly management financial package.



The Senior Financial Analyst supports the close process through analysis and review. Accounting ownership and final accounting entries remain with the accounting function.



Financial Modeling & Decision Support

Build financial models to evaluate business decisions, including:

• New customer opportunities

• Contract pricing

• Wage increases

• Customer price increases

• Hiring decisions

• Capital investments

• Equipment and technology investments

• Cost-reduction initiatives

• Changes in operating assumptions



Perform scenario and sensitivity analysis to show management how different assumptions affect revenue, profitability, EBITDA, and cash flow.



Business & Operational Analysis

Analyze financial and operating data to identify opportunities and risks involving:

• Labor

• Supplies

• Workers’ compensation

• Customer profitability

• Operating efficiency

• Pricing

• Overhead

• Productivity



Support management with ad hoc financial and business analysis as requested.



What Success Looks Like

The successful analyst does more than prepare spreadsheets.

For example, instead of reporting:

“Supply expense was $40,000 over budget.”

We expect analysis such as:

“Supply expense was $40,000 over budget. Approximately $18,000 resulted from higher purchasing in Market A, $11,000 resulted from vendor price increases, $7,000 appears related to purchasing volume above expected levels, and $4,000 remains unexplained and requires additional investigation.”

Your job is to help management understand what happened, why it happened, and where attention is required.



Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or related field.

• Minimum 4 years of relevant experience in FP&A, financial analysis, management accounting, or corporate finance.

• Strong understanding of the income statement, balance sheet, and cash-flow statement.

• Demonstrated experience with budgeting and forecasting.

• Demonstrated experience performing variance and root-cause analysis.

• Strong financial modeling skills.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.

• Ability to analyze large amounts of financial and operational data.

• Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

• Ability to work independently and investigate issues without requiring step-by-step instructions.

• High attention to detail and accuracy.



Preferred Qualifications

Experience with any of the following is helpful but not required:

• QuickBooks Online

• Fathom

• ERP or operational management systems

• Power BI or similar reporting tools

• Multi-location businesses

• Service businesses

• Labor-intensive businesses

• U.S.-based companies

• Remote international teams



The Person We’re Looking For

You are naturally curious about numbers.

When something changes significantly, your first reaction is to determine why.

You are comfortable challenging data that does not make sense.

You distinguish between an accounting error and a genuine change in business performance.

You can take a large amount of information and reduce it to the few things management actually needs to understand.

You don’t simply identify problems. You investigate them.

You are comfortable working directly with senior management and explaining financial information clearly and concisely.

You take ownership of your work and follow issues through to resolution.



Work Schedule

• Full-time

• 40 hours per week

• Remote

• Long-term position



The position will require regular working-hour overlap with U.S. Pacific Time for meetings and collaboration. Exact schedule will be discussed during the interview process.

Application Requirements



Please submit:

1. Resume/CV.

2. Brief description of your FP&A or financial analysis experience.

3. Description of a financial analysis you performed where you identified the underlying cause of a significant variance or business issue.

4. Your experience with budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling.

5. Your level of Excel proficiency.

6. Your desired hourly rate.



Skills Assessment

Final candidates will complete a paid financial analysis exercise.

Candidates will receive sample financial statements and operating information and will be asked to:

• Analyze a P&L.

• Review a balance sheet.

• Identify significant variances and potential issues.

• Perform cause-of-change analysis.

• Prepare a basic cash-flow forecast.

• Build a simple financial scenario.

• Summarize findings and recommendations for management.

The assessment is designed to evaluate analytical ability, financial judgment, Excel proficiency, and communication skills.

title: Revenue Intelligence & CRM Specialist
description:
About Spectrum



Spectrum Building Services of America is a commercial janitorial services company serving multi-location and portfolio customers across California, Arizona, Colorado, Washington and Oregon. Spectrum focuses on quality-oriented customers in property management, retail, automotive, healthcare, office/corporate and government/municipal environments.



The Role

We are seeking a curious, analytical and highly organized Revenue Intelligence & CRM Specialist to support Spectrum’s business-development system. This is not a traditional sales closer role and it is not primarily a data-entry role. Your job is to investigate target organizations and future opportunities, turn fragmented information into useful intelligence, and make that intelligence operational in HubSpot.

You will work behind Spectrum’s senior revenue leaders so they can spend their time on relationships, qualification, site walks, pricing, proposals, negotiation and closing rather than searching for information.



What You Will Do

• Research target companies and portfolios that fit Spectrum’s ideal customer profile and have meaningful multi-location or portfolio potential.

• Identify potential RFPs, contract renewals, procurement events, consolidations, expansion signals and other credible revenue opportunities.

• Investigate incumbent vendors, likely contract timing, service scope, facility counts, geography, procurement structure and buying process.

• Identify and verify facilities, operations, procurement, supplier-diversity, property-management and executive contacts who matter to a pursuit.

• Use public sources, procurement portals, company websites, LinkedIn and other approved resources to develop evidence-based account and opportunity intelligence.

• Create and maintain accurate Company, Contact and Deal records in HubSpot and move research into Spectrum’s defined revenue workflow.

• Prepare concise account briefs and opportunity briefs that tell senior leaders what is known, what is not verified, why the opportunity may matter and what should happen next.

• Monitor assigned opportunity sources and procurement channels, flag meaningful signals promptly and maintain research and next-action hygiene on assigned records.

• Escalate strong-fit opportunities, meaningful buying signals, conflicting information and data-quality issues to the Revenue 



System Owner.

How You Will Use AI

Modern AI tools are part of the job. You should be comfortable using AI to accelerate research, summarize documents, organize findings, draft account briefs and identify questions that deserve further investigation. AI output is never treated as verified simply because an AI system produced it.

• Verify material facts against reliable sources before entering or presenting them as facts.

• Clearly distinguish verified information, reasonable inference and unknown information.

• Use AI to increase the quality and speed of your work, not to generate large volumes of unverified data.



What You Will Not Own

Final qualification judgment, bid/no-bid decisions, pricing, proposal approval, customer commitments, contract negotiation and closing are owned by Spectrum’s senior revenue leaders. You provide the intelligence and CRM discipline that allow those decisions to be made well.



What We Are Looking For

• 2-5 years of experience in B2B research, sales operations, lead research, procurement research, competitive intelligence, business-development support or a closely related role is preferred.

• Excellent investigative research skills. You enjoy figuring out how organizations buy, who matters, what may be changing and where credible evidence can be found.

• Strong analytical judgment and the ability to synthesize information from multiple sources rather than simply copy data.

• Excellent written English and the ability to communicate findings concisely to senior business leaders.

• Ability to distinguish verified facts from assumptions, conflicting information and incomplete information.

• Strong attention to detail, organization, follow-through and deadline management.

• Comfort working in a structured CRM process and maintaining high data-quality standards.

• Practical proficiency with modern AI tools for research and knowledge work, combined with disciplined fact verification.

• Experience with HubSpot or a comparable CRM is strongly preferred. Experience researching RFPs, procurement, multi-location companies or facilities services is a plus.



How Success Will Be Measured

Quality and usefulness come before raw activity volume. We care more about producing intelligence that changes a pursuit decision or creates a credible opportunity than producing large lists of names.

• Quality and completeness of target-account research.

• Credible opportunities and procurement signals surfaced.

• Verified coverage of the people who matter to priority accounts and pursuits.

• Accuracy, completeness and timeliness of HubSpot records.

• Quality and usefulness of account and opportunity briefs to Spectrum’s revenue leaders.

• Ability to investigate ambiguous questions, document sources and communicate confidence or uncertainty.

• Responsiveness to priorities and consistent execution of Spectrum’s revenue process.



Reporting & Working Style

You will report to Leah, Spectrum’s Revenue System Owner. Tom and Isaiah are the senior leaders who use the intelligence you produce, but Leah manages your priorities, workload, quality standards and coaching. You should be comfortable working independently inside a defined operating system, asking good questions when information is unclear and documenting your work so others can act on it.



Why This Role Matters

Spectrum is building a disciplined, technology-enabled revenue engine rather than relying on ad hoc prospecting. The objective is not to create more activity. It is to consistently identify a smaller number of accounts and opportunities that deserve senior leadership attention and to reach those opportunities earlier and better prepared.



How to Apply

Please submit your resume and a brief note explaining why this type of investigative revenue work fits you. In your note, answer the following questions:

• Describe one research problem where the answer was not easy to find. How did you investigate it and verify what you found?

• Which AI tools do you use for research or knowledge work, and how do you prevent AI-generated errors from becoming business facts?

• Describe your experience with HubSpot or another CRM and how you maintained data quality.

• Give an example of a time you turned a large amount of information into a concise recommendation or brief for someone else.

Finalists should expect a short paid practical research exercise using a sample target account.

title: Creative Director for AI-Built Marketing Pages and Proposals (Claude Code or Codex)
description:
Job overview

Strategic Growth Architect is a marketing company, not the typical agency. We act as the marketing department for small businesses that do not have one of their own: full service, from strategic planning through to the pages,
s and campaigns that carry it out. That is why our clients matter so much to us: we are a partner to them, not an agency, and everything we hand them has to feel that way.



We work with each client to understand their needs, build their marketing plan, and turn that plan into briefs for the specific pieces the plan calls for: pages, proposals,
s, brand work. Those briefs are what you will turn into a client-facing deliverable the client can review, revise and approve, built with AI and directed by a person with a good eye. We are looking for that person. Start with a paid test project; if the work is good, you will get steady projects from us, and if it is great, a place on the team.





THE WORK



You will create client-facing review pages, proposals,
 drafts and other marketing pieces as portable HTML pages with their assets. We recommend Claude Code or OpenAI's Codex; a comparable AI tool that can create and revise files is fine.



Our briefs may include meeting notes, brand guidelines, source files and incomplete details. Use your tool to work through that context and make sound decisions about the result. You do not write code; the tool builds the page, and you direct it.



Think of yourself as the director: you shape the final result by directing the AI, reviewing its work and d
 what needs to improve.





YOU ARE



- Someone who notices when a page is dull, generic or not made for the client, and can say exactly what is wrong.

- A clear writer. You can read a paragraph of client-facing copy and cut what does not earn its place.

- Someone who directs an AI tool rather than accepting what it gives you: specific feedback, several rounds, and you check the result yourself.

- Someone who follows written instructions to the letter when it matters, such as how the work is packaged and handed in.

- Someone who has used an AI coding tool before, such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, and has your own access or is willing to set it up.

- Someone who says what you could not check or did not know, rather than hoping nobody notices.





YOUR MOST IMPORTANT RESPONSIBILITY



Make the client feel listened to. When they open the deliverable, it should be visually appealing, easy to read and clearly made for them. It should help them understand their options or take the next step.



Expect to personally inspect the actual pages and direct several rounds of revision. Remove repetitive explanations, generic filler and awkward layouts. Use AI to audit the work against the supplied requirements, then check the finished result with your own eyes.



We assess the quality of the work, the cost to reach an acceptable result and how much additional direction it needs. We do not reward long prompts or revision counts for their own sake.





PAY, AND WHAT COMES AFTER THE TEST



Invited applicants receive $30 USD for completing and submitting the test according to its instructions, whether or not we hire them. It is a fictional client brief; most people finish it in two to three hours. Completed test projects are paid through Wise within seven days of submission, regardless of the hiring decision.



After the test, if the work is good, there is a lot more. We have steady work and we want people we can rely on for it.



We begin with fixed-price projects, with the scope and price agreed before you start. For ongoing hourly work, we offer $10 to $20 USD per hour based on demonstrated quality, efficiency and independence. We evaluate the total cost of a finished, client-ready deliverable, not the hourly rate alone. You'll know and agree to the rate before starting each paid client project. Hours are flexible; you choose when you work and meet the agreed deadline.



Payment is through Wise. Per-project work is paid on approval of each project. Hourly work is paid on the 15th and the last day of the month.



Every deliverable is reviewed against the agreed brief. For fixed-price projects, payment is made once the work meets that brief and is approved. Revisions needed to bring it into spec are included in the agreed price. For hourly work, revisions count toward the approved time budget; ask before exceeding it.



Tools: if you do not have your own AI tool licence, we can provide one. What we look at is the total cost of a deliverable we can send to a client, your pay and the tool together, so bringing your own licence is reflected in what we pay you.





HOW TO APPLY



Apply through the OnlineJobs.ph application system. No long cover letter, introduction video or interview is needed. We want to see one thing you have already made with an AI tool, and how you got it there.



Send us one example of a deliverable you produced with an AI tool: a web page, a proposal, a landing page, an
, or similar. A link or the file itself. Share only work you have permission to show, with any confidential details removed.



Then tell us how you got there, in a few paragraphs:

1. Which AI tool you used, and whether you have your own access to it.

2. What the tool gave you at first, and what you saw that needed to change.

3. What you told it to change, how many rounds it took, and how the result improved.

4. What you checked yourself before you called it finished.



Also tell us:

- Your approximate availability for assignments.

- Whether you are interested in project work, part-time work, or eventually full-time work.

- Whether fixed-price projects to start, $10 to $20 USD an hour for ongoing hourly work, and payment through Wise work for you.





WHAT HAPPENS NEXT



We read every application ourselves and reply to everyone, usually within a week. If your example and your story show the eye and the judgment we are looking for, we will invite you to the $30 test project: a fictional client brief with the client's materials and a starter kit for your AI tool, with one hand-in. We review it the same way we review client work and tell you what we saw.



Do the test well and you will start getting paid client projects right away. Do them consistently well and we will talk about part-time or full-time work on the team. We would rather find one excellent person and keep them busy than keep interviewing.

You will normally receive the script, voice-over and instructions the previous day, usually by around:



18:00 Spain time / 00:00 Philippine time.



The finished video must normally be delivered by:



18:00 Philippine time / 12:00 Spain time.



Our normal publishing window is approximately 15:00–16:00 Spain time, so this gives us enough time to review the video before publication.



Please do not apply if you cannot consistently meet this delivery schedule.



Reliability with deadlines is extremely important for this position.



IMPORTANT – Automated Video Generation Is Strictly Prohibited



Please read this carefully before applying.



Using AI tools to assist your workflow is allowed and encouraged.



However, using automated video-generation workflows is strictly prohibited.



You may not take the script and upload it into tools such as Auraclipy or similar platforms that automatically generate the video, select stock footage, connect through APIs to Pixabay, Pexels or other stock libraries, and then simply correct the generated result afterward.



We have had bad experiences with this in the past, so there will be zero tolerance regarding this rule.



Footage and visual assets must be selected intentionally according to what is being explained in the script.



Using Pixabay, Pexels or other libraries manually is completely fine. What is prohibited is automating the editing and footage-selection process.



If we discover that automated video-generation software has been used during the test, the test will be rejected, payment for the test will not be issued, and the collaboration will be permanently cancelled.



Please only apply if you are comfortable working this way.



What We Expect



You should be able to:



Edit engaging long-form YouTube videos.

Understand the script before editing.

Find relevant B-roll, images and footage yourself.

Maintain good pacing and frequent visual changes.

Understand viewer retention.

Use CapCut, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or similar software.

Use AI tools intelligently without automating the entire editing process.

Follow references and established channel styles.

Work independently.

Meet daily deadlines consistently.

Communicate clearly.

Suggest improvements instead of simply waiting for instructions.



We value proactive people. If you see something that could improve the videos, retention or workflow, we want you to tell us.



Paid Test & Salary



Before starting the collaboration, there will be one paid test video.



Payment for the test video: $20.



The purpose of the test is to evaluate editing quality, pacing, footage selection, understanding of the script and ability to follow the required style.



If the test is successful, we will move into a 2-week trial period.



During those two weeks, you will be paid weekly at the normal salary rate.



Base salary:



$400/month



Paid as:



$100/week



After the trial period, the intention is to continue working together long-term.



There will also be performance-based bonuses once the channel has enough data.



The main bonus system will be based on audience retention. Because the channel is new, we first need to establish a normal retention baseline before setting specific targets.



Once we have enough data, clear and measurable retention targets will be established so strong editing performance can be rewarded fairly.



How to Apply



Please send:



A short introduction.

Your best long-form YouTube editing examples.

Your portfolio.

Which editing software you use.

Which AI tools you use.

Confirmation that you can commit to approximately 35 hours per week and 6 videos per week.

Confirmation that you can work with the delivery schedule described above.

Confirmation that you understand and accept our rule regarding automated video-generation software.



Start your application with the word EVERGREEN.



Any application that does not begin with the word EVERGREEN will be automatically rejected.



We are looking for someone who wants to become a long-term member of the team, not someone looking for a few isolated projects.

title: HubSpot RevOps Systems & Analytics Analyst (Ongoing, US Pacific Hours)
description:
We are an enterprise cybersecurity company (API, bot and AI security) looking for a RevOps Systems & Analytics Analyst to join our revenue operations team on an ongoing basis.



This is a hands-on execution role. We own the architecture and the decisions; you build, clean, reconcile and report. You will report to our Director of Revenue Operations and work from a single ticket queue, so priorities are always clear.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Build and maintain HubSpot properties across Companies, Contacts, Deals, Line Items and Quotes, with documentation

- Build workflows in draft for us to review and activate

- Execute data cleanup: dedupe worklists, value normalisation, backfills and association repairs, always with a dry run first

- Monitor our CRM integrations and raise a ticket with evidence when a sync breaks

- Build core reports and dashboards in the HubSpot custom report builder, and tell us whether a number moved because of the business or because of the data

- Write and fix SQL behind our warehouse reporting and reconcile it back to the CRM

- Prepare the monthly commission reporting inputs: pull the closed-won extract, reconcile revenue and term fields, and flag defects



WHERE WE DRAW THE LINE

You produce the worklist and the evidence; we make the call. Schema and architecture decisions, workflow activation, record deletion and merges, and commission sign-off stay with us.



WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

- 4+ years in revenue operations, CRM administration or business systems analysis

- 2+ years hands-on HubSpot administration, including the custom report builder

- HubSpot Academy certification in Revenue Operations or Reporting (please be ready to share as requested)

- Working SQL: joins, aggregations, CTEs, and debugging a query you did not write

- Strong spreadsheets: pivot tables, XLOOKUP, Power Query or equivalent

- You check counts and sample records before you write anything

- Professional written and spoken English

- Consistent availability during 9am-5pm US Pacific

- Your own reliable computer, a backup internet connection and a quiet workspace



NICE TO HAVE

- Salesforce administration or SOQL

- BigQuery or another cloud data warehouse

- HubSpot API or CLI

- Experience supporting a sales commission process



HOW WE HIRE

1. Short application. Please include answers to these two questions in your application:

   a) Describe a data cleanup you executed from someone else's spec. What was your dry-run process, and what did you escalate rather than d
?

   b) A dashboard shows pipeline down 20% week over week. How do you work out whether it is real?

2. A paid written exercise, about one hour. We send a spreadsheet of roughly 200 anonymised deals; you send back the integrity defects you found with counts, the SQL or formulas you used, what you would fix first and why, and what you would ask us before touching any of it. No access to our systems required.

3. A 45-minute call where you screen-share a report or dashboard you built in a portal you already work in.



HOW WE WORK

Weekly meetings to review our sprint board. Every request is a ticket. You post a short end-of-shift update: what you finished, what you are blocked on and who owns the unblock, and what is next. Escalating a question stops the clock; guessing does not. Structural and destructive changes are reviewed by us before they go live.



This is a long-term, full-time engagement and we would like to eventually bring the right person in-house.

title: Video Editor + Creative VA for Spreadsheet Template Business (YouTube, Pinterest, Canva) — Part-Time, Weekly Tasks
description:
Job Overview



Hi! I run TopSheets, a growing digital product business selling spreadsheet templates (Google Sheets + Excel) on Etsy and my own website. I'm looking for ONE reliable, detail-oriented VA to become my long-term creative right hand.



Right now, the biggest project is editing my catalog of YouTube tutorial videos. Alongside and beyond that, you'll create short-form social media content (reels/TikToks), Pinterest pins, and Canva listing mockups — the ongoing creative work that keeps the business running and growing.



This is a part-time role (roughly 10–15 hours/week) built around a weekly task list — I send you the list at the start of the week, you deliver by the end of the week. You choose your own hours. No time tracking, no fixed schedule. I care about finished work, not hours online.



What You'll Do



YouTube tutorial editing (current big project):



Edit screen-recording tutorial videos (8–20 min finished). I provide a rough cut with the audio, screen recording, and talking-head footage already synced and mistakes removed. You make it YouTube-ready: zoom-ins and highlight callouts on the cells/formulas being discussed, pacing polish, text overlays

Clean, simple editing style — NO flashy transitions, NO MrBeast-style effects. Think calm, clear, helpful

Cut 1–2 vertical Shorts from each tutorial

I handle thumbnails, descriptions, and publishing myself — your job ends at the finished export



Pinterest:



Design pins in Canva using my brand templates (static + video pins)

Deliver a set number of finished pins each week — I handle scheduling and descriptions myself



Canva / Listings:



Upgrade/create listing image sets for Etsy and my website (device mockups, feature slides)

Adapt existing graphics for German, Spanish, and French editions (I provide translations)

Cut short looping preview videos for Etsy listings



Social media content (growing part of the role):



Create short-form reels/TikToks showing our templates in use — aesthetic, satisfying, planner-community style content

I provide the screen recordings and brand kit; you bring the editing and the eye

As the tutorial catalog wraps up, this becomes a bigger share of the weekly list



Requirements



Proven video editing experience (Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, or similar) — portfolio required

Comfortable in Canva

Strong written English

Reliable internet and a computer that can edit 1080p video smoothly

Organized: consistent file naming, uses Google Drive, communicates proactively when something is unclear or delayed

Bonus (not required): experience with Pinterest graphics or planner/stationery-niche content



Pay & Process



Paid trial week: I will hire 3 candidates for a one-week paid trial ($50 flat). Everyone gets the same task list and the same raw footage. One person gets the ongoing role.

Ongoing: flat weekly rate of $75/week for approximately 10–15 hours of tasks, paid weekly via [Wise/PayPal/Payoneer]. Workload flexes week to week and balances out.

Long-term role. I'm building this business for years, and I want someone who grows with it.



How to Apply



Start your application with the word PIVOT so I know you read this posting.

Link 3–5 examples of videos you've edited. At least one should be a tutorial, screen-recording, or explainer-style video if you have one. Tell me in one line what YOU did on each (edited only? added graphics? full production?).

Link 1–2 examples of short-form vertical content you've made (Reels, TikToks, or Shorts). If you don't have any yet, say so honestly — but examples are a big plus.

If you have Canva design work (pins, social graphics, product images), link a portfolio or 2–3 examples.

In 2–3 sentences, tell me: what's one thing that makes a tutorial video easy to follow?

Link one Instagram or TikTok account (any brand) whose short-form content style you love, and tell me in one sentence why.

Tell me your experience level with Canva and Pinterest (it's okay if it's beginner — just be honest).



Applications that don't follow these steps will not be considered. Thanks, and I'm excited to meet you!

title: Real Estate Financial Analyst (Multifamily Underwriting)
description:
Location: Remote, Philippines 



Type: Part time, hourly contractor, as needed Hours: Flexible and project based. There is no set weekly schedule. Work comes in as deals come in, so some weeks may be busy and others quiet. Availability to respond within US Eastern business hours when a deal is active is important. Reports to: Principal / Acquisitions Lead



About the Role:



We acquire value-add multifamily properties in the United States, typically 100 or more units. This role supports the acquisitions process by building financial models, underwriting potential deals, and screening opportunities against our investment criteria. You will work directly with the principal and be a core part of how we decide which deals to pursue.

This is a hands-on analytical role. You will be trusted to turn raw deal information (offering memorandums, rent rolls, T12 financials) into clear, defensible numbers.



What You Will Do:



-Build and maintain underwriting models in Excel for multifamily acquisitions (100+ units, value-add strategy)

-Review offering memorandums, rent rolls, trailing 12-month operating statements, and broker packages

-Model current and pro forma income and expenses, renovation budgets, rent premiums, and stabilized returns

-Calculate and present key metrics: cap rate (going-in and stabilized), IRR, equity multiple, cash-on-cash, DSCR, and yield on cost

-Run debt scenarios (agency, bridge, bank) and sensitivity tables on rents, expenses, exit cap, and interest rates

-Screen incoming deals against our buy box and flag which ones merit a deeper look

-Research submarket rent comps, sales comps, and demographic data using online sources

-Prepare short deal summaries and investment memos for internal review

-Maintain a deal pipeline tracker with status, key metrics, and notes

`Continuously improve our model templates and underwriting process



What We Are Looking For:



Required:

-Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related field 2+ years of experience in financial analysis, modeling, or underwriting

-Strong Excel skills: building models from scratch, sensitivity tables, clean and auditable structure

-Solid understanding of real estate return metrics (NOI, cap rate, IRR, DSCR, equity multiple)

-Excellent written English and the ability to explain assumptions clearly

-Detail oriented and comfortable working independently with limited supervision Reliable internet and a quiet, dedicated workspace



Preferred:

-Experience underwriting US multifamily or commercial real estate

-Familiarity with US lending terms (Fannie/Freddie, bridge loans, LTV, amortization, IO periods)

-Exposure to CoStar, Yardi, RealPage, or similar data tools 

-Experience reading and interpreting rent rolls and T12 statements 

-Prior work with US-based clients or employers



How We Work:

-Clear direction on deal criteria and model standards up front

-Work is assigned deal by deal. You will get a deal package, a target turnaround, and an estimated hour budget for each one

-Async communication by default, with a call when a deal needs discussion



Hours tracked per deal and invoiced as work is completed:

-This works best for someone who has other clients or flexible commitments and wants steady but variable work

-Feedback on every deal so you learn how we think

-Opportunity to take on more responsibility as you demonstrate strong judgment



Compensation

$10 to $15 USD per hour depending on experience, paid weekly or biweekly via Wise or a similar platform. Rate reviews after 90 days and as responsibilities expand.



How to Apply:



Send the following to this
: 

1. Your resume

2. A brief note on your experience with financial modeling or real estate underwriting

3. A sample Excel model you have built (any asset type is fine, remove confidential data)



***Candidates who move forward will complete a short paid underwriting test using a sample deal package.

title: AutoCAD Architectural & MEP Drafter, US Construction Plans (Part-Time / Salary / Per-Project)
description:
LONGHORN HOME & LAND LLC

Central Texas custom home builder and land developer

 

 

THE SHORT VERSION

 

- Architectural and MEP drafting for custom homes, barndominiums, and light commercial in Austin, Texas

- Revit and/or AutoCAD. Residential and commercial. Wood frame and steel buildings. Full MEP.

- $3 to $7 per hour depending on experience, or per square foot on plan sets

- Part-time and per-project now, growing into full time for the right person

- Mostly on US Central time, with some flexibility

- We are hiring ONE drafter to be our go-to person, not a bench of freelancers

 

If that sounds like you, please read the whole posting. There are two code words in it that you need to include in your application.

 

We build custom homes, barndominiums, remodels, additions, and light commercial projects in the Austin, Texas area. We are looking for an experienced architectural and MEP drafter to work with us on a part-time, per-project basis.

 

This is ongoing work rather than a one-time job. We run multiple projects per year and we want one drafter we can rely on long term.

 

This is a contractor position, not employment.

 

 

WHY THIS JOB IS WORTH YOUR TIME

 

We want to be honest about what we are and are not offering.

 

We are not the highest paying job on this site. What we are offering is steady, long-term work with one builder instead of chasing one-off projects.

 

- ONE PERSON, NOT A ROTATING BENCH. We are hiring a single drafter to be our go-to for everything we build. You are not one of five people we assign work to at random.

 

- CONSISTENT WORK AS PROJECTS COME UP. We run multiple projects per year and we are growing. Once we are working well together, our intention is to build this into full time, forty hours a week, as our volume supports it.

 

- YOUR RATE GOES UP AS YOU PROVE OUT. We start at $3 to $7 depending on experience. Reliability, accuracy, and how little we have to redline your work are what move that number. We would rather pay one person more than manage five people.

 

- WE PAY FAST. Invoices are paid on schedule through Wise. We do not make people chase us.

 

- WE ANSWER YOUR QUESTIONS. You will have direct access to us by text and phone during our workday. You are not waiting three days for a reply from a project manager.

 

- WE PROVIDE CODE ACCESS. We maintain an ICC Digital Codes subscription and give you access. You are not buying tools to work for us.

 

- WE TELL YOU WHAT WE WANT AND WHY. You will get real feedback on your work, not silence. If something is wrong we tell you directly, and if something is good we tell you that too.

 

What we ask in return is attention to detail, honest communication, and that you actually read the documents we send you.

 

 

WHAT YOU WILL DRAFT

 

Residential and light commercial drawing sets, including:

 

- Floor plans, foundation and slab plans, roof plans

 

- Exterior elevations, building sections, wall sections and construction details

 

- Door and window schedules, interior elevations, cabinetry and millwork layouts

 

- Reflected ceiling and lighting plans

 

- Electrical and power plans: receptacles, switches, dedicated circuits, panel locations, smoke and CO detectors

 

- Plumbing plans: fixtures, supply routing, DWV, stacks, water heater, cleanouts

 

- HVAC and mechanical plans: equipment locations, duct routing, supply and return, exhaust, thermostats

 

- MEP coordination across all of the above

 

- 3D models and interior and exterior renderings

 

- Full construction document sets developed from our sketches, field measurements, redlines, and existing plans

 

You are not responsible for stamped engineering, engineering calculations, or licensed architectural services. When those are required, we engage a US-licensed architect or engineer. Your job is accurate, coordinated, buildable drawings.

 

 

WHAT WE NEED YOU TO BE GOOD AT

 

This job has two halves and we need both.

 

First, you must be able to design and lay out a plan well. A floor plan that works, flows, and looks right matters to us and to our clients.

 

Second, you must understand how a building actually goes together, and catch problems before they reach the field. Ductwork fighting with beams and ceiling systems. Plumbing running through structural members. Lighting conflicting with diffusers. Equipment placed with no service clearance. MEP penetrations hitting structure.

 

Required experience:

 

- Residential and commercial drafting. We need both, not only one.

 

- Stick-built American wood-frame construction

 

- Metal buildings and steel-frame construction. Barndominiums are a large part of our work.

 

- US construction document standards and sheet organization

 

- Revit and/or AutoCAD required. Chief Architect, SketchUp, Archicad, Lumion, Enscape, or Twinmotion are a plus.

 

- Ability to export to the CAD formats our engineers require: .dwg, .dxf, .rvt, .ifc, .pdf

 

IF YOU ARE READING THIS, INCLUDE THE WORD BARNDO IN YOUR APPLICATION. There is a second word at the very end of this posting. We need both.

 

 

BUILDING CODES

 

You do not need to know Austin area code from memory, and you do not need to buy anything. We maintain an ICC Digital Codes subscription and give you access to the code editions we hold.

 

Our subscription will not cover everything. Projects land in different jurisdictions with their own adopted codes, local amendments, and requirements we do not already have on hand. When that happens, you need to be willing to go find the answer. Look up the jurisdiction, read what applies, and learn a code you have not worked with before.

 

If your response to an unfamiliar code is to wait for someone to hand it to you, this position will frustrate both of us.

 

What we do require is that you actually draft to those codes. Ceiling heights, egress, stair and landing dimensions, window sizing and emergency escape openings, smoke and CO detector placement, receptacle spacing, required GFCI and AFCI locations, fixture clearances, ventilation and exhaust requirements, and framing and header calls where we provide them.

 

These need to be right in the drawings, not approximated. If you are unsure whether something meets code, look it up in the access we give you, or ask us. Do not guess, and do not carry a detail over from a previous project just because it worked somewhere else.

 

 

COMMUNICATION AND AVAILABILITY

 

- Fluent written and spoken English. You will be on calls and video with us directly.

 

- Reachable by text,
, phone, and video chat.

 

- WILLING TO USE WHATSAPP,
, OR A SIMILAR MESSAGING APP WITH US DAILY. Most of our day-to-day back and forth happens by text rather than
. A quick question about a dimension, a photo from the field, a redline we need eyes on. Tell us which apps you already use.

 

- A VIDEO INTERVIEW WITH YOUR CAMERA ON IS REQUIRED. During the call we will ask you to read a short technical paragraph aloud and talk through your own work. This job runs on phone and video calls about dimensions and details, and we need to be sure we can understand each other. If you are not willing to be on camera, this is not the right position for you.

 

- YOU WILL WORK MOSTLY ON US CENTRAL TIME, 8:00 AM TO 5:00 PM, MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY. In Philippine time that is roughly 9:00 PM to 6:00 AM, so this is a night shift for you on most days. We need you available during our workday, because plans move fast here and a question that waits 14 hours costs us a day on the schedule.

 

  We are not rigid about every single day. There will be days where the work is heads-down drafting with nothing to discuss, and on those days we do not care when you do it. But the majority of your days need to overlap with ours, and when we have an active set moving, we need you reachable during our hours.

 

  Please be realistic with yourself about this before applying. If working nights most weeks is not something you can sustain, we would both rather know now.

 

- RESPOND WITHIN ABOUT TWO HOURS during our working hours. Not the next business day. When we send a question, a redline, or an answer you were waiting on, work should resume that morning. A 24-hour round trip on every question adds weeks to a project, and our clients are not on that schedule.

 

- SEND PROACTIVE UPDATES ON PROGRESS. We should not have to ask where a set stands.

 

 

ASK QUESTIONS. DO NOT GUESS.

 

Our sketches and field notes will sometimes be incomplete or contradictory. When information you need is missing or does not add up, ask us. Do not fill the gap with an assumption and keep drawing.

 

A question takes us two minutes to answer. The same question, unasked, becomes a mistake that gets poured in concrete and framed in steel, and then it is expensive. There is a section further down that explains exactly what that costs us and what happens if it becomes a pattern.

 

You will never be penalized for asking, no matter how many questions you have or how basic they seem.

 

If you do have to proceed on an assumption to keep moving, write it on the drawing so we can see it. This is an obligation in our subcontract agreement, not a preference.

 

 

CAPACITY AND SCHEDULE

 

Tell us honestly how many hours per week you can commit and what you realistically need for a full set.

 

Be straight with that number. Do not pad it to leave yourself room for other clients, and do not shorten it to win the job. We build our own estimate of how long the work should take, we compare it to yours, and we settle on a date together. A number that is padded by a week is obvious to us, and it costs you credibility on the first project.

 

We move fast because we have made commitments to our clients. A realistic date that we agree on together is what we will hold you to.

 

 

REVISIONS

 

- Corrections to errors, omissions, or missed coordination in your own work are not revisions and are not billable. They are part of the deliverable.

 

- Each project includes a minimum of three rounds of client-driven revisions at no extra charge.

 

- Scope changes and revision rounds beyond that are billable and agreed in writing first.

 

 

CONTRACT, TAX, AND CONFIDENTIALITY REQUIREMENTS

 

Please read this section carefully before applying. These are firm requirements and they are not negotiable. If any of them is a problem for you, this is not the right position, and we would rather know now than after two interviews.

 

 

1) YOU WILL SIGN A MASTER SUBCONTRACTOR AGREEMENT (MSA) BEFORE ANY WORK BEGINS.

 

The MSA is our standing contract with you. Each individual project is then issued as its own work order under it, with the scope, price, and due dates in writing. The MSA covers, at minimum:

 

- Independent contractor status. You are a contractor, not an employee.

 

- Ownership and assignment of all work product to Longhorn Home & Land

 

- Confidentiality and non-disclosure of client and project information

 

- Data security and network requirements

 

- Revision and correction obligations

 

- Payment terms and schedule

 

- Turnaround commitments and what happens if a committed date is missed

 

- Termination and file handover

 

You will receive the full MSA to read before you sign. Please ask questions about it. We would rather explain a clause than have you sign something you did not read.

 

 

2) FILE AND WORK PRODUCT OWNERSHIP. PLEASE READ THIS ONE TWICE.

 

All drawings, models, renderings, and files you produce for us are the property of Longhorn Home & Land. This includes the native working files (.rvt, .dwg, .dxf, .skp, .pln, and rendering scene files), not only the exported PDFs. Native files are delivered to us at each milestone and at the end of every project, whether or not the project is completed.

 

You do not retain ownership, licensing rights, or any claim to the files. You may not withhold native files for any reason, including a payment dispute. You may not reuse our drawings, plans, models, or renderings in your portfolio, on your website, on social media, or in any application to another client without our written permission.

 

Please do not apply if you are not comfortable with this. Some drafters keep native files as leverage or as portfolio material. That does not work here, and it is the fastest way to end the relationship.

 

 

3) W-8BEN OR W-8BEN-E IS REQUIRED BEFORE YOUR FIRST PAYMENT.

 

Individuals file W-8BEN. If you work through a registered company or entity, W-8BEN-E. We cannot pay you until we have it on file.

 

 

4) YOU ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR YOUR OWN TAXES.

 

We do not withhold anything, we do not provide benefits, and we do not provide equipment or software. You cover your own hardware, software licenses, and internet. We cover code access as described above.

 

 

5) CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA SECURITY.

 

Our clients' plans, home addresses, and project details are private information, and protecting them is a contract obligation. You must:

 

- Work on a private, password-protected network. No public Wi-Fi, no shared connection, no internet cafe, no hotel or coworking network.

 

- Work on a device you personally own or control, password or biometric locked, with current security updates. Nobody else uses that device while our files are on it.

 

- Keep all project files in the shared drive we provide. Not on personal cloud accounts, personal
, third-party file transfer sites, messaging apps, or flash drives.

 

- Never share login credentials we issue you with anyone.

 

- Never paste, upload, or submit our drawings, models, sketches, client addresses, or project information into any third-party AI tool or online service that stores or trains on what you submit. This includes ChatGPT, AI drafting and rendering services, and free online converters. If you want to use an AI tool in your workflow, ask us first and we will tell you yes or no.

 

- Tell us within 24 hours if a device or account holding our files is lost, stolen, accessed by someone else, infected, or if you suspect it has been compromised.

 

- Never discuss, post, or share any client information, project location, or drawing with anyone.

 

- When a project ends, or when we ask, permanently delete our files from all your devices, accounts, and backups, and confirm in writing that you did.

 

 

6) BE HONEST ABOUT YOUR SCHEDULE.

 

Tell us the truth about your workload. If you take on more than you can deliver and our plans sit while you finish someone else's, we will find out, and we will end the agreement. We are not asking you to work only for us. We are asking you to commit only to what you can actually deliver.

 

 

PAY

 

$3 to $7 per hour depending on experience. We raise it as you prove out. Reliability, accuracy, and how little we have to redline your work are what move that number.

 

On plan sets we also pay per square foot, which is how plan work is commonly priced in the US. The rate is agreed per project before work begins, plus flat fees for assignments outside a plan set.

 

For the right person we are open to a salary arrangement instead of hourly, once we have worked together long enough to know what the volume looks like.

 

Payment is made through Wise or your preferred method. When you apply, tell us your hourly rate and your per-square-foot rate.

 

Every work order states its rate, its scope, and its payment terms in writing before you start. Nothing about how or when you get paid will be a surprise, and you will have the chance to ask about all of it before you sign anything.

 

 

WHAT AN ERROR ACTUALLY COSTS, AND WHAT HAPPENS

 

We would rather you understand this before you apply than after you are hired.

 

When a drafting mistake is not caught, it does not stay on paper. It gets ordered, cut, poured, and welded. We find out at the framing stage that a header is in the wrong place, an opening is the wrong size, or a beam does not land where the plan says it does. On a custom home, a single error of that kind costs between $5,000 and $30,000 to correct, and it can push a client's move-in date by weeks.

 

That money comes out of our business, and the damage to our reputation with that client lasts a lot longer than the invoice.

 

This is why we are particular about who we hire, and why we would rather answer twenty questions a day than receive one set built on assumptions.

 

WHAT HAPPENS IF IT GOES WRONG

 

We are not going to send you a bill for a framing error. That is not realistic and it is not what we are asking for. What we will do is this:

 

- You correct every error, omission, and coordination failure in your work at your own expense, on your own time, with no extension to the deadline. This is in our subcontract agreement.

 

- We may charge the cost of correcting your work against amounts we owe you, as our subcontract allows.

 

- If it keeps happening, or if we find you have been filling in gaps instead of asking, we end the agreement.

 

We want to be fair about this, so we will say it plainly. We are not looking to punish anyone for a mistake. Everyone makes them, and an honest error that you flag yourself is a completely different thing from a gap you papered over and said nothing about. The first one we fix together. The second one ends the relationship.

 

 

DAILY PROGRESS REPORT

 

While you have active work with us, send a short progress note at the end of each of your working days. Three or four lines is plenty:

 

- What you completed

 

- What you are working on next

 

- Anything blocking you, or any question you need answered to keep moving

 

We are not asking for this to check up on you. We are asking because when we know where a set stands, we can answer your questions before they cost you a day. A drafter who goes quiet for four days and then delivers is a drafter we cannot plan around.

 

 

ABOUT AI

 

Use AI to help you learn something, look something up, or check your own work. That is your business and we do not mind.

 

What we will not accept is AI writing your messages to us. Not in your application, not on your first day, not ever.

 

Here is the reason. Almost all of our daily communication is text and
. When we ask how a set is going, we need to know what you actually think. Whether you are stuck. Whether something in the sketch does not make sense. Whether you are going to miss a date. An AI-written update is confident, polished, and tells us nothing. We find out you were stuck three days later, when the schedule is already gone.

 

Three broken sentences telling us you are confused about a dimension are worth more to us than a perfect paragraph that hides it.

 

So:

 

- Your application, your video, and every message after you are hired must be your own words. AI writing is easy to spot and we read with that in mind. More importantly, you will be on a live video call discussing what you wrote. If your writing is polished and you cannot talk about it in your own words, that is an immediate no, and there is no way around it.

 

- This applies from your first message and every day after. If your writing reads like a language model and your calls do not sound like the same person, that ends the working relationship.

 

- Never put our drawings, models, sketches, client addresses, or project information into any AI tool or online service that stores or trains on what you submit. This is a term of our subcontract.

 

TO BE CLEAR ABOUT OUR STANDARD, BECAUSE THESE TWO THINGS WORK TOGETHER:

 

Your English needs to be good enough that we understand you the first time, in writing and on the phone. If we have to schedule a call to work out what a message meant, or ask you three times to explain something, that costs us more time than the work saves. Strong written and spoken English is a requirement of this position.

 

At the same time, it has to be your English. We are not asking for perfect grammar or advanced vocabulary. Plain, clear, direct sentences are exactly right. Small mistakes are fine and we will never mention them.

 

We need to understand you, and we need to know that it is actually you. A polished AI paragraph fails the second test. Unclear writing fails the first. Write simply, in your own words, and you will pass both.

 

 

HOW TO APPLY

 

Reply with this subject line:

 

DRAFTER, [YOUR NAME], [WORD 1] [WORD 2]

 

Two code words appear in this posting. Include both, in order, in your subject line and in the first line of your message.

 

We do this because this job is about reading a full set of documents carefully and catching what is in them. If you cannot get through one job posting, the drawings will be a problem.

 

Applications missing either word, or missing answers to any question below, are not reviewed.

 

PLEASE ANSWER EVERY QUESTION. Number your answers so we can follow them.

 

 

Q1. How many years have you drafted US residential plans? US commercial plans?

 

Q2. Which software do you use daily, and which version?

 

Q3. Have you drafted metal building or steel-frame projects such as barndominiums, shops, or mixed-use metal buildings? Describe one.

 

Q4. Have you drafted stick-built wood-frame homes? Describe one.

 

Q5. Have you drafted full MEP plans covering electrical, plumbing, and HVAC, or only architectural? Please be honest. We ask this specifically.

 

Q6. Give one example of a coordination conflict you caught in a drawing set before it reached the field, and how you resolved it.

 

Q7. Our hours are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM US Central, which is roughly 9:00 PM to 6:00 AM your time. Are you willing and able to work that schedule consistently? Have you worked a US night shift before, and for how long?

 

Q8. Are you comfortable with Longhorn Home & Land owning all work product including native .rvt and .dwg files, with no portfolio use without written permission? Yes or no.

 

Q9. How many hours per week can you commit to us, and how many other clients are you currently drafting for?

 

Q10. What is your realistic turnaround on a complete construction document set for a 2,000 square foot custom home, working from our sketches?

 

Q11. What is your hourly rate in USD? Do you also price per square foot, and if so, what is your rate?

 

Q12. Provide three references: name, company, and
 or phone. We will contact them about your drafting and rendering work.

 

Q13. Attach or link a portfolio showing full construction document sets, not only renderings. We want to see sheets: plans, sections, details, schedules, and MEP.

 

Q14. Describe a project where you produced a plan set from hand sketches, field measurements, or redlines rather than an existing CAD file. What information was missing, and how did you handle it?

 

Q15. Are you willing to complete a paid test assignment and walk us through your file on a video call? Yes or no.

 

Q16. Which messaging apps do you use? WhatsApp,
, Viber, or something else. We will be texting you most days.

 

 

REQUIRED: SHORT VIDEO

 

APPLICATIONS WITHOUT A VIDEO LINK ARE NOT REVIEWED. This is not optional and we do not make exceptions.

 

Record a video of yourself, 60 to 90 seconds, and include the link in your reply. Upload it as an unlisted YouTube video, or as a Google Drive link set so that anyone with the link can view it.

 

Requirements:

 

- Your face visible and well lit, speaking directly to the camera

 

- One continuous take. No editing, no cuts, no voice-over.

 

- Your own voice. Not a reading by someone else, not text-to-speech, not AI-generated.

 

Please do these three things, in this order.

 

STEP 1. Say your full name, then say both code words from this posting out loud.

 

STEP 2. Read this aloud, exactly as written:

 

"The slab is 48'-0" x 32'-0" with a 4" thickened edge at the garage openings. Wall studs are 2x6 at 16" o.c., and the top plate sits at 10'-4 1/2". The roof is a 6/12 pitch with a 2'-0" overhang. Supply the header schedule before framing, and confirm the rough opening for the 3'-0" x 6'-8" exterior door."

 

STEP 3. Then, without reading from anything, answer this in your own words for about thirty seconds:

 

"Tell me about a drawing set you worked on where the information you were given was wrong or missing, and what you did about it."

 

We are not judging your accent. We are checking that we can understand each other clearly on a phone call about dimensions, because that is how this job runs every day. Speak at a normal pace and do not over-prepare. Step 3 is meant to be unscripted, and we would rather hear you think than hear you recite.

 

 

SKILLS VERIFICATION: REQUIRED

 

Before we award any real project, every shortlisted candidate completes a paid test assignment. This is not optional and there are no exceptions, regardless of how strong your portfolio or references are.

 

Here is exactly what it involves:

 

- We send you a hand sketch, rough field measurements, and basic project notes. This is the same kind of information you will actually receive from us on a live job.

 

- You produce three sheets from it: exterior elevations with 3D views, a foundation plan, and a second floor framing plan with a staircase elevation.

 

- You also submit a written, numbered list of every discrepancy, missing dimension, and conflict you found in the sketches, with the question you would ask us about each.

 

- The deadline is 3 days.

 

- You are paid a flat fee for this assignment whether or not we hire you. We do not ask anyone to work for free. This is a fixed fee for a reduced-scope sample exercise built from rough field sketches. It is not our rate for production plan sets and you should not read it as one. Rates for real project work are negotiated with you separately, per project, before any work starts.

 

- You will then get on a video call and walk us through your own file, live, sharing your screen. We will ask you why you made specific decisions.

 

We want to be clear about why we do this. Most of the work you will do for us starts as a sketch on paper, a photo of a napkin, or a set of measurements taken in the field, rather than as a clean file handed to you. We need to see that you can take incomplete information, ask the right questions, and produce a coordinated and buildable set.

 

A portfolio shows us finished work. It does not show us whether you personally did it, or whether you understand it.

 

The screen-share walkthrough is part of the test. If you cannot explain your own drawing decisions, we will know.

 

 

LAST TWO THINGS

 

APPLY POINTS: please use at least 6 Apply Points when you send your application. Applications sent with fewer than 6 will not be reviewed. We are hiring one drafter for ongoing work, and we want to hear from people who are choosing this job rather than applying to everything.

 

YOU REACHED THE END. THE SECOND WORD IS PECAN. Include both BARNDO and PECAN in your application, in your subject line and in the first line of your message.

 

If you are sending the same application to many job posts, this is where it stops. We read every reply, and a message without both words tells us everything we need to know.

 

We look forward to hearing from the people who actually read this.

title: Senior Product Designer – Vendor Panels & Mobile App | 2–3 Week Project
description:
We are looking for a highly skilled Product Designer / UX Designer for a focused 2–3 week project.



The main task is to redesign and improve our vendor panels / dashboards and, if time allows, also improve selected parts of our mobile app.



Our platform, InfoAlanya, includes bookings and services such as transfers, tours, restaurants, beauty, dental and more.



We are looking for someone who is not only strong visually, but especially good at:



complex user flows

vendor/admin dashboards

booking logic

information hierarchy

mobile UX

interaction design

usability

edge cases

clean and modern product design



The goal is to make our vendor panels much easier, cleaner and more professional to use.



You will work on areas such as:



vendor dashboard structure

booking management flows

statuses and actions

forms and inputs

navigation

mobile responsiveness

UX improvements

possibly selected app screens and flows



All designs should be created in Figma and be clear enough for our developers to implement.



We expect the project to take approximately 2–3 weeks, depending on experience and speed.



We are looking for someone who can work independently, understand an existing product quickly and suggest better UX solutions rather than only following instructions.



Please send:



Your portfolio

Examples of dashboards, admin panels or mobile apps you have designed

Your availability for the next 2–3 weeks

Your expected project rate or hourly rate

How many hours per week you can work



Experience with booking platforms, marketplaces, travel, transport or ride-hailing products is a big plus.



Important:

We care more about product thinking, flows and usability than just making screens look pretty.

title: Trailer Management Admin
description:
GH Logistics (AJG Transport) is a high performance freight brokerage and asset based logistics company specializing in dry van and refrigerated freight. We move quickly, but we move with structure. Our operation is built on real-time visibility, disciplined execution, and clear communication. We take pride in keeping freight organized, assets accounted for, and operations running cleanly from pickup to delivery.



If you’re someone who enjoys structured execution, asset visibility, and maintaining operational accuracy behind the scenes, you’ll feel right at home here.



Role Overview

You support the Trailer Manager in overseeing a fleet of 1000+ trailers across multiple carriers and terminals. You play a critical role in ensuring every trailer is accounted for, properly assigned, compliant, and operational. This is not a passive data-entry role. You’re the person who keeps the fleet picture accurate, coordinates trailer repair concerns, and flags problems before they cost us time and money.



You should be familiar with common trailer repair and maintenance issues and understand how to coordinate practical solutions with drivers, terminals, vendors, and maintenance teams. If you thrive on structure, take pride in clean records, and don’t let things slip through the cracks, this role was built for you.



What You’ll Be Doing

• Monitor, update, and reconcile trailer locations across the network on a daily basis

• Coordinate with route supervisors, internal team, dispatchers, carriers, drivers, and terminals to ensure accurate trailer assignments and timely movement

• Track trailer availability, maintenance schedules, and repair status

• Identify trailer issues, assess their operational impact, and coordinate the appropriate repair solution

• Maintain accurate and up-to-date trailer documentation (registrations, inspections, tags, insurance)

• Support reporting on trailer utilization, downtime, and compliance

• Identify discrepancies, missing updates, or unreported trailer statuses and escalate promptly

• Assist in improving internal trailer tracking systems for better visibility and accuracy

• Execute processes consistently with strong attention to detail

• Collaborate cross-functionally with dispatch, compliance, and maintenance teams



What Success Looks Like

• Trailer locations and statuses are consistently accurate and fully reconciled

• Assignments, availability, and movements are properly documented and updated in real time

• Maintenance, repair, and compliance records are complete and up to date

• Trailer defects and repair needs are identified early, properly communicated, and resolved efficiently

• Discrepancies are identified early and resolved before impacting operations

• Reporting on utilization and downtime is clean, accurate, and actionable

• Communication across departments is clear, timely, and structured



Who We’re Looking For

• Experience in fleet management, trailer maintenance coordination, logistics coordination, truck or trailer repairs, dispatch, or similar live operational roles (not general admin work)

• Familiarity with common dry van and refrigerated trailer repairs, defects, and maintenance concerns

• Ability to understand trailer repair issues, determine the appropriate next steps, and coordinate solutions

• Knowledge of common trailer components and issues, such as tires, brakes, lights, doors, landing gear, air lines, electrical systems, refrigeration units, and structural damage, is strongly preferred

• Strong attention to detail with high accuracy in tracking and record-keeping

• Organized and capable of managing multiple data points across systems and teams

• Clear and professional communication skills across departments

• Familiarity with platforms such as Samsara, LoadStop, or similar tracking systems is a plus

• Proactive mindset, able to identify and address issues before they escalate

• Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills in a fast-paced environment

• Minimum 45 WPM typing speed

• Proficient in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and Logistics tools

• Reliable internet connection and fully equipped remote work setup

• Team oriented, coachable, and aligned with structured processes



Schedule & Work Setup

• Full time permanent remote role

• Direct Hire to a US Company (not agency or BPO)

• Current needed shifts: Tuesday - Saturday 8 PM - 6 AM CDT

90%+ of collectable AR collected each month.

title: Video Editor & Social Media Content Creator Part-Time | Remote
description:
Ohana Plumbing is a Sydney-based plumbing company. 

We’re looking for a creative, reliable and proactive Video Editor & Social Media Content Creator to join our team on a part-time, remote basis.



You do not need to film content. Our team in Sydney will provide raw video footage, job-site videos, before-and-after photos, talking-head videos and other brand materials.



Your job is to turn that raw content into professional, engaging social media content that educates homeowners, builds trust in the Ohana Plumbing brand and helps generate enquiries.



Key Responsibilities



• Edit raw plumbing and job-site footage into polished marketing content.

• Create Instagram Reels, TikToks,
 videos and YouTube Shorts.

• Review raw footage and identify the strongest clips and moments.

• Create attention-grabbing hooks within the first 1–3 seconds.

• Add captions, music, transitions, graphics, sound effects and other visual elements where appropriate.

• Turn plumbing topics into simple, interesting and educational content homeowners can understand.

• Create before-and-after and problem/solution videos from our projects.

• Edit talking-head and educational videos featuring our plumbers and team.

• Repurpose one piece of raw footage into multiple pieces of social content.

• Create different versions and angles from the same project where appropriate.

• Follow Ohana Plumbing's brand guidelines and maintain a consistent, professional visual style.

• Make amendments based on feedback from our team.

• Suggest new hooks, content concepts, trends and creative ideas.

• Organise content and deliver completed videos within agreed deadlines.



We want someone who can take something that may seem like an ordinary plumbing job and turn it into content people actually want to watch.



What We’re Looking For



• Previous experience in video editing and social media content creation.

• A strong portfolio demonstrating Reels, TikToks, Shorts, paid ads or business marketing content.

• Strong understanding of short-form content, hooks, retention and storytelling.

• Ability to make educational content visually engaging.

• Experience with Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, CapCut or similar editing software.

• Good written and spoken English.

• Strong attention to detail, particularly spelling and captions.

• Good creative judgement when selecting footage.

• Ability to follow brand guidelines while still bringing creative ideas to the team.

• Reliable internet connection and ability to download/upload large video files.

• Organised, dependable and able to work independently.

• Comfortable receiving feedback and making revisions.



Bonus Skills



These aren't essential, but we'd love to hear from you if you also have experience with:



• Meta/Facebook ad creatives

• Direct-response video editing

• Creating multiple hooks or variations for paid advertising

• Canva or graphic design

• AI video and content creation tools

• Motion graphics

• YouTube editing

• Content strategy

• Home services, trades or construction businesses



What Success Looks Like



We don't want someone who simply cuts clips together.



We're looking for someone who understands why someone stops scrolling, why they keep watching and what makes them take action.



You should be comfortable looking at raw footage and thinking:



"How can I turn this into a piece of content that a Sydney homeowner would actually stop and watch?"



If you're creative, reliable, enjoy experimenting with social media content and want to work with a growing Australian home-services brand, we'd love to hear from you.



To Apply



Please send:



• A short introduction about yourself

• Your video editing portfolio

• Examples of Reels, TikToks, Shorts or paid social creatives you've edited

• The editing software you use

• Your availability and preferred working hours

• Your expected hourly or monthly rate



Please also tell us which video in your portfolio you believe performed best creatively and why.
